documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

65M, retired accountant, here to set up primary care. Comes alone, brought his bottles.

Blood pressure has been treated for years on lisinopril 20 mg; he checks it at the pharmacy kiosk now and then and says it's usually in the 130s. On atorvastatin 40 mg for cholesterol, no muscle aches. Takes both in the morning and rarely misses. No chest pain, no breathlessness on the stairs, no leg swelling. No headaches, no vision change. Never had a stroke or a TIA that he knows of.

PMH: hypertension, hyperlipidemia.
PSH: cataract surgery 2021, done at an eye practice; vision fine since.
Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily.
Allergies: none to medications.
FH: father had an ischemic stroke at 74. Mother with high blood pressure. Brother has coronary disease.
SH: married, lives with his wife. Retired from accounting. Smoked about 35 pack-years and stopped in 2017, no relapse. A drink once or twice a month. Walks the neighborhood most mornings.

Exam: Well-appearing, organized historian. BP 134/82. Clear lungs, regular rhythm without murmur. No carotid bruits. Abdomen benign, no pulsatile mass. Legs without swelling, pedal pulses present. Gait normal.

A/P
1. Essential hypertension: close to goal on lisinopril 20. Continue. BMP today.
2. Hyperlipidemia: atorvastatin 40, fasting lipid panel today.
3. Former heavy smoker: meets criteria for yearly low-dose CT; ordered. One-time aortic ultrasound ordered as well.
4. Health maintenance: hep C screen today. Colonoscopy per his account about 4 yrs ago and normal, will confirm from records. High-dose flu and PCV20 given today. PHQ-2 0.

Follow up in 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your labs from Monday
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Dennis, good to meet you on Monday. Your bloodwork came back fine. Kidney function, potassium, liver tests and blood counts are normal. The LDL cholesterol is where we want it on the atorvastatin, and your A1c shows no sign of diabetes. The hepatitis C screen was negative. No changes. The CT and the aorta ultrasound orders are in, and scheduling will call you.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text: LOW-DOSE CT CHEST, LUNG CANCER SCREENING. Baseline exam. Indication: 65-year-old former smoker, 35 pack-years, quit 2017. Technique: helical low-dose acquisition without contrast. Findings: No pulmonary nodules. Airways patent. No consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal, no pericardial effusion. No enlarged mediastinal or hilar nodes. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening in 12 months.

reports.text: ULTRASOUND, ABDOMINAL AORTA, SCREENING. Indication: male former smoker, age 65. The abdominal aorta is visualized from the diaphragm to the bifurcation. Maximum outer-to-outer diameter 2.1 cm in the infrarenal segment. No focal dilation or aneurysm. Common iliac arteries normal in caliber.
reports.conclusion: Normal caliber abdominal aorta, 2.1 cm. No abdominal aortic aneurysm.

documents.title: CT and ultrasound results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Dennis, both studies were normal. The lung screening CT showed no nodules, so we repeat it once a year. The aorta measured normal size with no aneurysm, and that one does not need repeating. Enjoy the fall.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD (received from a regional hospital; date of service 5/25/2025)

CC: left foot dragging

HPI: 68-year-old man brought in by his wife, who saw him catching the toes of his left foot as he walked this afternoon. He has no pain anywhere. Describes the left leg as hard to pick up. No headache, no speech trouble, no arm symptoms. No previous stroke or TIA.

PMH: hypertension, hyperlipidemia. PSH: cataract surgery (2021).
Home meds: lisinopril, atorvastatin.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father with ischemic stroke at 74; mother hypertensive; brother with CAD.
Social: retired accountant. Ex-smoker, 35 pack-years, quit 2017. Alcohol once or twice monthly.

Exam: Awake, alert, oriented x3. CN II-XII intact. Strength 5/5 bilateral upper extremities and right lower extremity; left lower extremity 3/5 with mildly increased tone. Sensation intact throughout. Normal finger-to-nose bilaterally; upper-extremity reflexes normal.

CT head noncontrast: small right frontal hypodensity, no hemorrhage.
Labs: CBC, BMP and INR unremarkable.

Impression: acute ischemic stroke, right frontal lobe, with left leg weakness.
Disposition: admitted to the hospital for stroke care.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY (regional hospital)
Admitted 5/25/2025, discharged 5/27/2025.

Principal diagnosis: acute ischemic stroke, right frontal lobe.
Other: hypertension, hyperlipidemia.

Course: Presented with left leg weakness noticed by his wife. Noncontrast CT head showed a small right frontal hypodensity without hemorrhage. Monitored on the medical floor with neuro checks. The left leg weakness improved steadily over two days; by discharge he was walking the hallway with physical therapy, still catching the left foot occasionally. Fasting lipids and A1c were in range on his current regimen.

Discharge medications (unchanged):
- lisinopril 20 mg daily
- atorvastatin 40 mg daily
Allergies: NKDA.

Disposition: home with his wife. Outpatient physical therapy for the left leg. Follow up with his PCP within 1 to 2 weeks and with neurology clinic in about 6 months. Return for any new weakness, numbness, speech or vision change.

documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PHYSICAL THERAPY, INITIAL EVALUATION (date of service 6/9/2025)
Referral: inpatient stroke team, left lower extremity weakness after right frontal ischemic stroke 5/25/2025.

Subjective: wants to get back to his morning walks without his foot catching. No falls.
Objective: Left hip flexion and ankle dorsiflexion weak compared with the right. Gait with intermittent left foot drag, more with fatigue and on turns. Independent indoors without a device. Transfers independent.
Assessment: gait deviation from left leg weakness, good potential.
Plan: twice weekly for 8 weeks; strengthening, gait training, balance; home exercise program.

Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Neurology Clinic Letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY CLINIC (regional hospital stroke clinic), visit 11/17/2025

Dear colleague,

I saw Mr. Rousseau, 68, for his planned follow-up six months after his right frontal ischemic stroke. His daughter came with him and supplied most of the history. Across the past week she has seen an abrupt change in him: he forgets recent conversations, drifts off task, and cannot lay out his day the way he always has; she stresses he has been a meticulous planner his whole life. He himself mentions only that the left side feels mildly weak.

Background: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, the May stroke. Cataract surgery 2021. Medications lisinopril and atorvastatin. NKDA. Father had an ischemic stroke at 74, mother hypertension, brother coronary disease. Former smoker (35 pack-years, stopped 2017), rare alcohol, retired accountant.

Examination: alert, though flat and apathetic in manner. Language fluent without aphasia. Cranial nerves normal. Mild drift of the left arm and leg. Sensation normal.

Noncontrast head CT today: small, well-circumscribed right frontal hypodensity at the site of the known infarct, no new lesion.

Impression: vascular dementia following the right frontal infarct, with predominantly executive and attention problems and apathy.

Recommendations: continue blood pressure and cholesterol treatment as you are. Please check vitamin B12 and TSH if not recent. A baseline cognitive screen in your office would be useful. I advised that he not drive. Family to help with finances and medications. I will see him again in about six months.

Sincerely,
Stroke neurology

reports.text: CT HEAD WITHOUT CONTRAST. Indication: acute vertigo, ataxia. Comparison 11/17/2025. Findings: Small well-circumscribed hypodensity in the right frontal lobe, unchanged, consistent with old infarct. No intracranial hemorrhage. No mass effect. Posterior fossa without hemorrhage or hydrocephalus; fourth ventricle midline. No extra-axial collection.
reports.conclusion: No hemorrhage. Old right frontal infarct, unchanged.

ED PHYSICIAN RECORD, regional hospital (date of service 6/1/2026)

CC: dizziness and nausea

HPI: 69M with HTN, HLD, right frontal ischemic stroke 5/2025 and vascular dementia, brought by wife. Abrupt onset this morning of spinning dizziness with nausea and difficulty staying upright. The spinning persists whether he lies still or fixes on something. Mild headache started at about the same time. No fall, no head injury, did not pass out. History partly from wife given his cognitive impairment.

Meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily. NKDA.
PSH: cataract surgery 2021.
FH: father ischemic stroke at 74, mother HTN, brother CAD.
SH: retired accountant; quit smoking 2017 after 35 pack-years; alcohol rarely.

Vitals: BP 160/90, HR 78, T 36.8 C.
Exam: Horizontal nystagmus that persists with visual fixation. Speech mildly slurred, language intact. Dysmetria on right finger-to-nose. No facial asymmetry, no pronator drift.

CT head noncontrast: no hemorrhage; old right frontal infarct unchanged.
Labs: CBC, BMP, INR unremarkable.

Assessment: acute vertigo with nystagmus not suppressed by fixation, dysarthria and right-sided dysmetria; concern for central (posterior circulation) cause.
Plan: admit for MRI and stroke care.

reports.text: MRI BRAIN WITHOUT CONTRAST. Indication: acute vertigo, dysmetria. Comparison CT 6/1/2026. Technique: multiplanar multisequence imaging including diffusion-weighted images. Findings: Small focus of restricted diffusion in the right cerebellar hemisphere with corresponding ADC hypointensity, compatible with acute infarct. Chronic infarct in the right frontal lobe. No hemorrhage on susceptibility images. No mass effect. Ventricles normal in size. Normal flow voids.
reports.conclusion: Small acute infarct, right cerebellar hemisphere. Chronic right frontal infarct.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospitalist
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY, regional hospital
Admission 6/1/2026, discharge 6/3/2026.

Principal diagnosis: acute ischemic stroke, right cerebellar hemisphere.
Secondary: prior right frontal ischemic stroke (5/2025), vascular dementia, hypertension, hyperlipidemia.

Hospital course: Admitted from the ED with acute vertigo, nausea, gait instability, mild dysarthria and right-sided dysmetria; head CT without hemorrhage. MRI showed a small acute right cerebellar infarct and the old right frontal infarct. Vertigo and nausea settled over the first 36 hours. Walking with PT and his wife at the bedside by day 2; steady enough for home with supervision. Lipids and A1c in range.

Discharge medications:
- NEW: aspirin 81 mg daily
- lisinopril 20 mg daily (unchanged)
- atorvastatin 40 mg daily (unchanged)
Allergies: NKDA.

Disposition: home with wife. PCP visit within 1 week. Stroke neurology clinic in about 6 to 8 weeks. Return for recurrent dizziness, new weakness, speech or swallowing trouble.

documents.title: Neurology Clinic Letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
STROKE NEUROLOGY CLINIC, visit 7/20/2026

Dear colleague,

Mr. Rousseau returned with his wife seven weeks after his right cerebellar infarct. The dizziness is fully gone and he is back to walking with her daily. Family describe his memory and initiative as unchanged from the winter.

Medications: aspirin 81 mg, lisinopril 20 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg. NKDA.

Exam: alert, apathetic but engaged. No nystagmus. Finger-to-nose accurate on both sides. Gait steady, able to tandem a few steps.

Impression: recovered from a small right cerebellar infarct; prior right frontal infarct with vascular dementia.

Plan: continue aspirin, atorvastatin and lisinopril. Return in 6 months.

With best regards,
Stroke neurology
